'''Hervé This''' ({{IPA|fr|ɛʁve tis|lang}}; born 5 June 1955), sometimes named '''Hervé This-Benckhard''' or '''Hervé This vo Kientza''', is a French physical [[chemist]] who works for the [[Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique]] at [[AgroParisTech]], in Paris, France. His main area of scientific research is [[Molecular gastronomy|molecular and physical gastronomy]], that is the science that studies culinary transformations.

== Career ==
With the late [[Nicholas Kurti]], he coined the scientific term "Molecular and Physical Gastronomy" in 1988, which he shortened to "[[Molecular Gastronomy]]" after Kurti's death in 1998.<ref>{{cite book |last= This |first= Hervé |year= 2005 |title= Molecular Gastronomy: Exploring the Science of Flavor |publisher= Columbia University Press |isbn= 0-231-13312-X |url-access= registration |url= https://archive.org/details/moleculargastron0000this }}</ref> After graduating from [[ESPCI Paris]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espci.org/fr/anciens/eleves/95/|title=Les ingénieurs de la 95e promotion de l'ESPCI Paris}}</ref> he obtained a PhD from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]], under the title ''{{lang|fr|La gastronomie moléculaire et physique}}''.<ref>[http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=179563 La gastronomie moléculaire et physique = Molecular and physical gastronomy] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100228053614/http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=179563 |date=28 February 2010 }} {{in lang|fr}}</ref> He has written many scientific publications,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://search.worldcat.org/search?q=au:Herve%CC%81+This&qt=results_page|title=au:Hervé This – Search Results|website=search.worldcat.org}}</ref> as well as several books on the subject, which can be understood even by those who have little or no knowledge of chemistry, but so far only four have been translated into English. He also collaborates with the magazine ''{{lang|fr|Pour la Science}}'' (the French edition of ''Scientific American''), the aim of which is to present scientific concepts to the general public. Member of the Académie d'agriculture de France since 2010, he was the president of the Section "Human Food" for 9 years. In 2004, he was invited by the French Academy of sciences to create the "Food Science & Culture" Foundation, of which he was appointed the Scientific Director. That same year, he was asked to create the Institute for Advanced Studies of Taste ("Hautes Études du Goût") with the University of Reims Champagne Ardenne, of which he is the president of the Educational Program. In 2011, he was appointed as a consulting professor of AgroParisTech, and he was also asked to create courses on science and technology at [[Sciences Po]] Paris. 
On 3 June 2014, he was asked to create the "International Center for Molecular Gastronomy AgroParisTech-Inrae",<ref>{{cite web | url=https://icmpg.hub.inrae.fr/international-activities-of-the-icmpg | title=International activities of the International Centre of Molecular Gastronomy – Inrae-AgroParisTech International Centre of Molecular and Physical Gastronomy/Centre International de gastronomie moleculaire et physique AgroParisTech-Inrae }}</ref> to which he was appointed director. That same day, he announced the creation of the International Journal of Molecular Gastronomy<ref>{{cite web | url=https://icmpg.hub.inrae.fr/international-activities-of-the-icmpg/molecular-gastronomy | title=Journal of Molecular and Physical Gastronomy – Inrae-AgroParisTech International Centre of Molecular and Physical Gastronomy/Centre International de gastronomie moleculaire et physique AgroParisTech-Inrae }}</ref>.{{fact|date=August 2022}}

[[File:Hervé This at Dublin Institute of Technology, Cathal Brugha Street, 2011.jpg|thumb|Hervé This at Dublin Institute of Technology, Cathal Brugha Street, 2011 with student Ciarán Elliott demonstrating how to achieve a greater volume when whipping egg whites.]]

Some of his discoveries include "uncooking eggs",<ref>Hervé This. Can a cooked egg white be  uncooked ? The Chemical Intelligencer (Springer Verlag), 1996 (14), 51. </ref>  a "dispersed system formalism" (DSF), "dynagels", in situ quantitative nuclear magnetic, resonance spectrometry, "Chocolate Chantilly", a foam made of chocolate without eggs (and also cheese Chantilly, butter Chantilly, foie gras Chantilly...), new ways of cooking eggs, which he called "eggs at 6X°C"{{Citation needed|date=May 2013}} (around 65&nbsp;°C, the white begins coagulating, but not the yolk), and more generally a large number of colloidal systems. He also found that beating an egg white after adding a small amount of cold water considerably increases the amount of foam produced. Every month he adds one new "invention" in the ''Art et Science'' section of the website of the chef [[Pierre Gagnaire]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pierre-gagnaire.com/francais/cdthis.htm|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101126142239/http://pierre-gagnaire.com/francais/cdthis.htm|url-status=dead|title=Art et Science|archivedate=26 November 2010}}</ref>

Although his main focus is on physical chemistry, he also attributes great importance to the emotional aspect of cooking, as the title of one of his books shows: ''Cooking is love, art, technique''.{{fact|date=August 2022}}

Aside his scientific work, the latest "political" work by Hervé This has been the invention (in 1994) and the promotion of [[synthetic cooking]], also called [[Note by Note cuisine]] – the next stage in the application of science to the kitchen after molecular cooking (i.e. a technical way of producing food using equipments imported from laboratories). Note by note cooking involves taking the molecules that compose ingredients used in cooking, and using these as the raw ingredients for making dishes. "If you use pure compounds, you open up billions and billions of new possibilities," Mr This said. "It's like a painter using primary colors or a musician composing note by note."{{fact|date=August 2022}}

As part of the 2011 International Year of Chemistry, The French Embassy in Ireland in association with the Institut Français, the Alliance Française Dublin, the Lycée Français d’Irlande and the French Trade Commission UBIFRANCE put on a number of lectures around Dublin, Ireland where Hervé This performed demonstrations and promoted the new concept of 'note by note' cuisine.<ref>[http://www.ambafrance-ie.org/spip.php?article1703 2011 – Molecular Gastronomy – Hervé This]</ref>

In 2025, he was awarded the [[Sonning Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://via.ritzau.dk/pressemeddelelse/14235742/gastronomic-artist-is-awarded-the-sonning-prize-2025?publisherId=13561237&lang=da|title=Gastronomic artist is awarded the Sonning Prize 2025 &#124; Københavns Universitet|website=via.ritzau.dk}}</ref>

* 1993 : ''les Secrets de la casserole'', Éditions Belin

* 2006 : ''La cuisine c'est de l'amour, de l'art, de la technique'', Odile Jacob
* 2007 : ''Construisons un repas'', Odile Jacob
* 2007 : ''De la science aux fourneaux'', Pour la Science/Editions Belin
* 2007 : ''Kitchen Mysteries: Revealing the Science of Cooking'' (translator: Jody Glading), Columbia University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-231-14170-3}} or 023114170X
* 2007 : ''Alchimistes aux fourneaux'', Flammarion
* 2009 : ''Building a Meal: From Molecular Gastronomy to Culinary Constructivism (Arts and Traditions of the Table: Perspectives on Culinary History)'' (translator: Malcolm DeBevoise), Columbia University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-231-14466-7}}
* 2009 : ''Cours de gastronomie moléculaire n°1 : Science, technologie, technique (culinaires) : quelles relations?'', Quae/Belin, Paris.
* 2011 : ''Cours de gastronomie moléculaire n°2 : Les Précisions culinaires'', Quae/Belin, Paris.
* 2012 : ''La cuisine note à note en douze questions souriantes'', Belin, Paris.

* 2014 : ''Mon histoire de cuisine'', Belin, Paris.
